definitions.explanation: A situation where two propositions or principles, each appearing valid in itself, are mutually contradictory; an irreconcilable conflict between two equally reasonable positions.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}{成長|せいちょう}と{環境|かんきょう}{保護|ほご}は{二律背反|にりつはいはん}の{関係|かんけい}にあると{言|い}われる。
examples.english: Economic growth and environmental protection are said to be in an antinomical relationship.

examples.japanese: {自由|じゆう}と{平等|びょうどう}の{二律背反|にりつはいはん}は{哲学|てつがく}の{重要|じゅうよう}なテーマだ。
examples.english: The antinomy between freedom and equality is an important topic in philosophy.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}と{家庭|かてい}の{二律背反|にりつはいはん}に{悩|なや}んでいる。
examples.english: I'm struggling with the conflict between work and family.

notes:
ORIGIN: This is a Japanese translation of the philosophical term "antinomy" (from Greek). It was notably used by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant to describe contradictions in pure reason.

STRUCTURE: {二|に} (two) + {律|りつ} (laws/principles) + {背|はい} (against) + {反|はん} (oppose). Literally: two laws opposing each other.

USAGE: Used in philosophical, academic, and general contexts to describe situations where two principles or goals conflict with each other.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{二律背反|にりつはいはん}の{関係|かんけい} (an antinomical relationship)
・{二律背反|にりつはいはん}に{陥|おちい}る (to fall into a contradiction)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{矛盾|むじゅん} (contradiction)
・ジレンマ (dilemma)
・{板挟|いたばさ}み (caught between two conflicting forces)
